title: Understanding RowHammer Under Reduced Refresh Latency: Experimental Analysis of Real DRAM Chips and Implications on Future Solutions
problem: RowHammer mitigations based on preventive refresh incur growing performance and energy overheads as DRAM technology scaling reduces the activation threshold for bit-flip induction. The interaction between refresh latency and RowHammer vulnerability in real DRAM chips has not been rigorously characterized.
motivation: Shrinking DRAM technology nodes drastically lower the RowHammer threshold, forcing more aggressive preventive refreshes that impose significant performance, energy, and area overhead on future mitigation mechanisms.
method: The authors perform the first experimental characterization of refresh-latency vs. RowHammer interactions on 388 real DDR4 chips from three manufacturers, varying preventive refresh (tRFM) latency below nominal values. They find that refresh latency can be reduced by 64% with only a 0.54% increase in required refresh count. Building on these findings, they design PaCRAM (Partial Charge Restoration for Aggressive Mitigation), a mechanism that reduces tRFM for preventive refreshes and compensates by slightly increasing refresh frequency, thus lowering the performance tax of five state-of-the-art RowHammer defenses.
key_novelty: First silicon-validated demonstration that preventive DRAM refresh latency can be substantially reduced (by 64%) with minimal extra refresh count, enabling a new low-cost operating point for RowHammer mitigation.
contributions: First rigorous experimental study of refresh latency vs. RowHammer characteristics on 388 real DDR4 DRAM chips
Demonstration that preventive refresh latency can be reduced by 64% at the cost of only 0.54% more refreshes
PaCRAM mechanism that reduces performance and energy overheads of five existing RowHammer mitigation schemes

metrics.other: Refresh latency reduced by 64%; preventive refresh count increase of only 0.54%; performance and energy improvements over 5 state-of-the-art mitigations

limitations: Experiments are limited to DDR4 chips; applicability to DDR5 and future DRAM generations with different cell architectures requires further study.
primary_theme: RowHammer mitigation via reduced refresh latency
